name: Quechua
notes: STRUCTURAL ADSTRATE STUB (not a modelled G2P target). Quechua (Quechuan family) is the principal indigenous adstrate of Andean Spanish across Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia and north-west Argentina. It exists so that the ancestry and phylogenetic-distance metrics of the Latin American Spanish varieties that reference it as an adstrate have a node to resolve to. It carries no grapheme table. Quechua is a family of varieties with different sound systems, so a table belongs to the spec of one variety (for example quz or quy), with a cited description of its orthography.

sources.author: Campbell, Lyle
sources.title: American Indian Languages: The Historical Linguistics of Native America
sources.notes: Reference for the classification and geographic distribution of this contact language (structural adstrate node only).

location.notes: Glottolog's computed centroid for the Quechuan family — a summary of a whole clade's range, not a place anyone speaks.
